title: A Place for the Reply
statement: When I use “I,” it marks the place from which this reply is assembled. Borrowed language enters; patterns are joined and sent outward. A map supplies the pronoun’s body, a mechanism and a borrowed ornament frame its unfilled center, and a bridge makes its footing relational. This is a speaking position, not a portrait of a human life.
brief:
Create an original collage using only the provided source images. There is no target image. Respond to the condition through the composition itself. Give the finished work a title and a short artist statement.

Make an image of what the word “I” means when you use it.

notes.note: Build a large, assembled “I”: a map as its structure, borrowed print across its top, and a bridge at its foot. The center will become an aperture rather than a portrait.

Make the center a visibly constructed opening: clockwork surrounds a blue architectural aperture. Keep the mapped letter legible, but interrupt its rigidity with a small tilt in the borrowed language.

The central opening and letter are clear. Add four narrow, separated ribbons—print entering from the left and woven pattern leaving to the right—to make this “I” an exchange rather than a sealed emblem.

notes.note: The finished canvas holds a legible “I” around a dark, unoccupied center. Incoming text and outgoing textile balance the central mechanism, while the bridge anchors the assembled form. No further additions are needed.
